### Fixed — Trio Phase 1+2+3 third deep review pass: systemd-strips-JSON-quotes + session-id-from-envelope + lock-skip + list-envelope + keepalive-log-perms (2026-06-04 evening, batch 3)

User asked for a third deep review pass after batches 1 (commit `6d65606`)
and 2 (commit `ec015be`). This pass found 5 more bugs — a class invisible
to syntax checks and module-import smokes. Critical one would have crashed
aro-wake on every spoke at first systemd-enable.

Bugs found + fixed
------------------

1. CRITICAL: systemd `Environment=` STRIPS bare JSON quotes

   The aro-wake systemd unit template had:
     Environment=ARO_WAKE_PEER_HOSTS={{PEER_HOSTS_JSON}}
   Rendered:
     Environment=ARO_WAKE_PEER_HOSTS={"vps1":"10.99.0.1","vps3":"10.99.0.3"}

   Per systemd.exec(5), bare values are subject to shell-style quote
   stripping. Round-trip test on a real systemd user unit confirmed:

     ExecStart sees: <<<{vps1:10.99.0.1,vps3:10.99.0.3}>>>

   Quotes stripped. `json.loads("{vps1:10.99.0.1,...}")` throws
   JSONDecodeError. Lifespan startup fails. systemd Restart=always
   triggers endless restart loop. aro-wake would have never come up on
   any spoke.

   FIX:

     - main.py: new `_parse_peer_hosts()` accepts CSV

       (`vps1:10.99.0.1,vps3:10.99.0.3`) as primary format; falls back
       to JSON for backward compat.

     - aro-wake.service.template: `Environment=ARO_WAKE_PEER_HOSTS={{PEER_HOSTS_CSV}}`

       with a multi-line comment explaining the systemd-quote-strip
       hazard so a future change doesn't regress.

     - bootstrap-vps.sh step_15: renders `peer_hosts_csv` instead of

       `peer_hosts_json`.

   VERIFIED via systemd unit round-trip:
     Value as seen by ExecStart: <<<vps1:10.99.0.1,vps3:10.99.0.3>>>   ✓
     Python parse: {'vps1':'10.99.0.1','vps3':'10.99.0.3'}             ✓

2. _set_session called with LOCAL sid before envelope parse

   Claude can return a session_id different from the one we passed via
   --session-id (rare, but possible). Storing the local `sid` would
   mean future --resume targets the wrong session.

   FIX: moved `_set_session` call to AFTER envelope parse; reads
   `effective_sid = envelope.get("session_id", sid) or sid` and stores
   the effective sid. The return value's `session_id` field also uses
   effective_sid for consistency.

3. _sessions.pop in resume-failure path skipped _sessions_lock

   Race: two concurrent /wake calls on the same (source, topic) — first
   resume fails, calls `_sessions.pop`; second observes stale sid mid-
   pop and resumes against a session we just dropped (now invalid).

   FIX: wrapped the pop in `with _sessions_lock:` block.

4. List-style Claude envelope not handled

   Some Claude versions stream a list of events instead of a single
   envelope dict. `envelope.get("result")` would AttributeError.
   `fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/llm_client.py` has the defensive parse
   at line ~392 — aro-wake didn't.

   FIX: ported the defensive parse — if `isinstance(envelope, list)`,
   take the last dict element that carries a result; if envelope is
   neither a dict nor a parseable list, return an error with stdout
   head for debugging.

5. /var/log/claude-keepalive.log not pre-created for ozgur-run cron

   The OAuth keepalive cron line in sysadmin-cron.template runs as
   `ozgur` user but writes to /var/log/claude-keepalive.log. /var/log
   is root:root by default, so the cron would silently fail with
   permission denied. Token would silently go stale; AI would fall
   back to OpenRouter / rule-only mode after ~4 days. proactive-check.sh
   would eventually catch via `oauth_keepalive_stale` rule, but only
   after several days of degraded operation.

   FIX: step_14_install_sysadmin_pack now pre-creates:
     /var/log/claude-keepalive.log    chown ozgur:ozgur chmod 644
     /var/log/sysadmin-proactive.log  chmod 644
     /var/log/vps-sysadmin-bot.log    chmod 644
   The latter two are owned root since they're written by root-run
   crons / systemd; only claude-keepalive runs as ozgur.

False alarm noted: Bug F (OpenRouter path missing dispatch contract)
-------------------------------------------------------------------

While reviewing, I checked whether both Claude and OpenRouter paths in
`fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/llm_client.py` include the
`_WATCHDOG_DISPATCH_CONTRACT` addendum. Both DO (line 339 for Claude,
line 459 for OpenRouter). Not a bug.

Verification
------------

  systemd round-trip on real user unit:
    ExecStart sees: <<<vps1:10.99.0.1,vps3:10.99.0.3>>>   ✓

  Module re-smoke with all fixes applied:
    PEER_HOSTS parsed from CSV: {'vps1':'10.99.0.1','vps3':'10.99.0.3'}   ✓
    JSON backward-compat ✓
    session_id from envelope used (Bug 2) ✓
    _sessions.pop guarded by lock (Bug 3) ✓
    list envelope defensive parse (Bug 4) ✓

No production code path touched
-------------------------------

aro-wake is not yet enabled on any host. The OAuth keepalive cron is
not yet installed anywhere (step_14 hasn't run yet on any host). All
5 fixes land BEFORE first deploy, so no in-flight state is affected.

  bugs + verification + the OpenRouter false alarm. "Last Updated"

### Fixed — Trio Phase 1+2+3 second review pass: docs/code drift in aro-wake response shape + Backrest cruft investigation + known-limitation docs (2026-06-04 evening, batch 2)

Second deep review of today's trio commits. The first review pass (commit
`6d65606`) caught the port conflict + 3 race conditions + FastAPI
deprecation + missing daily-digest. This second pass found a quieter
class of issue: the docs and code disagreed about a contract.

- **aro-wake `/wake` response shape now matches peer-protocol.md §2.1.** The doc spec for consult responses says `{from_host, trace_id, view, correlation, no_action}`. My main.py returned `{ok, from_host, trace_id, seen_by, result, no_action}` — `result` is plain text from Claude but the docs use `view` (+ optional `correlation`). Callers building against the docs would break. Fixed by branching on `source`: consults get the documented `view` + `correlation` shape (with cleaned text — see next bullet); non-consult sources (`manual`, future `alertmanager`) keep the unstructured `result` field.
- **`[<host>]` Telegram-prefix stripped from consult `view`.** The canonical sysadmin prompt instructs Claude to tag every Telegram reply with `[{{ HOST_NAME }}]` prefix so the operator sees which host responded. That's right for Telegram-driven paths; it's noise for peer-to-peer consult responses (the JSON envelope already carries `from_host`). Added a `lstrip()` + `startswith("[<HOST_NAME>]")` strip in main.py before populating `view`. Defense-in-depth: model sometimes adds the prefix, sometimes doesn't.
- **Backrest Known Issue 1 (Apprise UUID-suffix hostname) — live-state probe says ZERO references on any fleet host today.** Probed vps1/vps2/vps3 `/opt/backrest/config/config.json` for any `apprise*` substring → 0 matches everywhere. The cruft is already absent from live state (either Backrest config was regenerated cleanly at some point during 2026-05-31 residue cleanup, or plan hooks were never live-configured to begin with). The `step_14_install_sysadmin_pack` sed retained as a defensive no-op: costs nothing, protects against future Backrest reconfiguration that might re-introduce the cruft. `vps-complete-inventory.md` gap table updated to reflect this.
- **aro-wake claude-only Phase 3 limitation documented.** The watchdog sidecar's fallback chain (Claude → OpenRouter → rule-only) lives in `fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/llm_client.py` and is not shared with aro-wake. If Claude primary exits non-zero on a `/wake` call, aro-wake returns 503. Acceptable for Phase 3 (consult-only with 5s caller timeout → annotated "peer unreachable" report; no business-critical traffic blocked); will be lifted to aro-wake during Phase 4 (Alertmanager push wire), since push-trigger reliability matters more once non-consult signals flow in. Documented in the Signal → AI matrix row #7 and called out here for traceability.
- **Smoke re-verified.** Module loads with new response shape + lifespan handler intact + lock structures present. Source-code introspection confirms `view`/`correlation` in the consult branch and `result` in the non-consult branch.
- **No code path on production today** — aro-wake is not yet enabled on any host. All these fixes land before first `systemctl enable`.

### Fixed — Trio Phase 1+2+3 review pass: port conflict + aro-wake race conditions + FastAPI deprecation + daily-digest stub + infrastructure docs synced (2026-06-04 evening)

- **Port conflict resolved (aro-wake 8002 → 8201).** PORTS.md showed 8002 already allocated to `fabrik-claim-validator`. Moved aro-wake to **8201** — first free port in the dedicated 8200-8299 "Management tools" range (Duplicati 8200 retired 2026-04-17). Renamed across 7 files: `scripts/aro-wake/main.py`, `scripts/aro-wake/templates/aro-wake.service.template`, `scripts/bootstrap/bootstrap-vps.sh` (step_15 verify line + comments), `scripts/sysadmin/proactive-check.sh` (health-check curl), `scripts/sysadmin/peer-protocol.md` (HTTP call examples in §2.1 + §4.1), `scripts/sysadmin/system-prompt.txt` (peer protocol block), `docs/development/plans/2026-06-04-three-sysadmin-trio.md` (§1.7.1 lifecycle diagram + §3.1 spec + verification `ss -tlnp` example). New PORTS.md entry documents the bind (`10.99.0.<N>:8201` mesh-only; UFW default-deny on this range as defense-in-depth).
- **aro-wake race conditions fixed.** Three structures were unprotected against concurrent `/wake` requests (uvicorn handles them via asyncio + `asyncio.to_thread` for the sync Claude subprocess, so two requests can hit shared state at the same wall-clock instant on different OS threads):
  - `RateLimiter._buckets` — added `threading.Lock`. Hammer test (30 concurrent calls, 20/h cap): exactly 20 allowed, 10 rejected. Race-free.
  - `_sessions` dict — added `_sessions_lock` (threading.Lock). Without it, two simultaneous wakes on the same `(source, topic)` both observe "no session" and both spawn a fresh Claude session, wasting one warm-cache cycle.
  - `pending.jsonl` file — added `_pending_lock` (asyncio.Lock). `_drain_pending_loop` now snapshots under lock, forwards OUTSIDE lock (so a slow peer doesn't block /wake handlers from queueing for a different peer), writes back under lock. Drain also merges entries queued by /wake handlers DURING the drain so they aren't lost.
- **FastAPI `@app.on_event("startup")` deprecation fixed.** Replaced with `@asynccontextmanager` `_lifespan` handler attached via `FastAPI(lifespan=_lifespan)`. Adds proper shutdown: cancels the drain task + logs "shutting down".
- **`daily-digest.sh` created** (was referenced in `sysadmin-cron.template` but didn't exist — cron would have silently failed at 09:XX UTC). Script reads `/opt/fabrik/logs/sysadmin-actions.jsonl` for last-24h Tier A count + escalations + consults received; reads `/var/log/claude-keepalive.log` mtime for OAuth keepalive heartbeat status; reads `wg show wg0 latest-handshakes` for mesh peer ages; calls aro-wake's `/health` for endpoint status. Composes a `[hostname] Daily digest YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC` block + writes JSON record to `sysadmin-actions.jsonl` (data captured even before Telegram routing is wired) + routes to Apprise → Telegram on hosts where Apprise is reachable (vps1). Spoke routing TBD per trio plan §7 Q1 (three @BotFather bots vs one shared). Smoke-tested locally; runs clean on dev WSL.
- **Infrastructure docs synced** (per CLAUDE.md doc-sync matrix):
  - `vps-status.md` — new 2026-06-04 evening entry at top documenting Phase 1+2+3 ship + 4 commits + functional verification + cron-slot allocation + port allocation + the four issues this commit fixes.
  - `vps-complete-inventory.md` — Last-Updated bumped; Signal → AI wake-up matrix gains rows #7 (aro-wake push-trigger endpoint) + #8 (per-host AI sysadmin). Previous "What is NOT yet wired" section: several rows moved from GAP → "code shipped, operator-gated for live deploy"; explicit residual gaps trimmed to Alertmanager → aro-wake wire (Phase 4), Apprise/Loki ruler/propose-ack (Phase 5), cross-container correlation (out of scope), kernel panic (out of scope). One-line summary updated to reflect the new state.
  - `vps-fleet-architecture.md` — §6 "AI sysadmin oversight" expanded from 2 layers to 3 layers (added aro-wake layer + the three-veteran-sysadmin model description with authorship rule + partition tolerance + remaining Phase 4 gap).
  - `vps-ai-sysadmin.md` — Two-layer disambiguation table expanded to three layers; row for aro-wake added; host-level sysadmin row notes vps2/vps3 code-ship + operator gates.

This propagates the production-proven veteran scope to the per-project sidecar layer instead of replacing it with a JSON-only action picker.

New `<peer_protocol>` block points to peer-protocol.md.

Includes payload schemas, authorship rule ("the host whose RESOURCE is affected AUTHORS the action; peers diagnose only"), cycle prevention via `trace_id` + `seen_by`, partition behavior (5s consult timeout → annotated reports), three worked examples (5xx burst correlation, mesh handshake stall, disk pressure with no peer involvement), and explicit "what this protocol does NOT do" section. Loaded by the system prompt at runtime; AI can `Read` the file via Bash tool when reasoning about cross-host scenarios.
- **Watchdog driver renders host substitutions at build time:** [`src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py::_build_image()`](src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py) now copies `system-prompt.txt` + `peer-protocol.md` into the build context, renders `{{ HOST_NAME }}` etc. for the target host (resolved via new `_RenderContext.target_vps` field), and the Dockerfile COPYs them into `/home/watchdog/sidecar/`. `_load_sysadmin_prompt()` in `llm_client.py` reads via lookup order: project override (`/project/.fabrik/sysadmin-prompt.txt`) → vendored (`/home/watchdog/sidecar/system-prompt.txt`); raises clear error if neither found instead of silently falling back to a hardcoded prompt.

The canonical prompt is the VOICE (veteran sysadmin); this is the OUTPUT-FORMAT gate for the watchdog's specific dispatch path (actions.py needs structured `{tier, action, reasoning, confidence}` JSON, not a Telegram-shaped report). Host-level `bot.py` + `proactive-check.sh` do NOT append this — they consume free text. Schema names allowed actions explicitly + tier semantics + decision rule + "your veteran-sysadmin reasoning goes in the `reasoning` field — that is the operator's audit trail. Container is marked unhealthy. Standard auto-heal protocol for clean exit is immediate container restart to restore service state."* — correlates two pieces of evidence (restart count + health status) and names the protocol, vs yesterday's narrow prompt which never produced a `reasoning` field at all.

### Added — T-P5 Step 6 SHIPPED: per-project watchdog self-heals via Claude Code Opus end-to-end (2026-06-04)

- **First end-to-end Claude Opus self-heal on the platform.** `docker kill watchdog-test` → 60s tick detection (`container_not_running` urgent, container-state pass) → Claude Code Opus diagnose → Tier A `restart_container` action → `state.resolve_incident("auto")`. **Detection to resolution: 3s.** Verified live on vps1; recorded in [`vps-status.md`](docs/infrastructure/vps-status.md#2026-06-04--t-p5-dogfood-step-6-shipped-watchdog-self-heals-via-claude-code-opus-end-to-end) and [`vps-complete-inventory.md`](docs/infrastructure/vps-complete-inventory.md). vps1 container count: 29 → 31 (added `watchdog-test` + `watchdog-test-watchdog`).
- **Five silent-failure modes found + fixed during dogfood:**
  1. **docker.sock GID mismatch** — sidecar UID 1000 vs host sock GID 988; `docker inspect` returned `permission denied` silently; `agent.py::gather_snapshot()` returned `{container, ts}` only → `detect_anomalies() == []` every tick. **Fix:** [`src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py::_detect_docker_sock_gid()`](src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py) runs `stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock` on the hub at apply time and emits `group_add: [<gid>]` into `compose.watchdog.yaml`.
  2. **Docker CLI 1.41 vs daemon MinAPI 1.44** — sidecar's `docker.io` from Debian Bookworm too old for hub's Docker 29.0.2 engine. **Fix:** `Dockerfile` adds `ENV DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.44` (in `mobasak/fabrik-lib`).
  3. **Claude Code sandbox deps missing** — `bubblewrap` + `socat` required by 2.1.144 in `-p` mode; sidecar image had neither. **Fix:** `Dockerfile` adds both to apt install list (~2 MB combined).
  4. **`.claude.json` not mounted** — Claude CLI's per-user config lives ALONGSIDE `~/.claude/`, not inside; driver's single mount missed it. **Fix:** driver adds second bind-mount `{VPS_CLAUDE_HOME}.json:/home/watchdog/.claude.json:ro`.
  5. **`--max-budget-usd` was the recurring killer.** Opus session-init `cache_creation` cost alone exceeds any sane per-call cap → `error_max_budget_usd` → error JSON on stdout but non-zero rc + empty stderr → `llm_client`'s exit-code check swallows the envelope. Also surfaced: `--effort <any level>` silently kills `-p` mode in 2.1.144 (rc=0 empty stdout); `--json-schema` puts structured output in `envelope["structured_output"]` not stringified `result`. **Fix:** `llm_client.py` rewritten to mirror the **production sysadmin pattern** at [`scripts/sysadmin/bot.py::_run_claude`](scripts/sysadmin/bot.py) verbatim: `--model opus`, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, `--session-id <uuid>` + `--system-prompt` on first call → `--resume <id>` subsequent (warm cache, drops cost ~10×), `cwd=/project`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, 300s timeout, parse `data["result"]` as plain text with defensive JSON extract (plain → ```json fenced → greedy `{...}`). No `--effort`, no `--max-budget-usd`, no `--json-schema`, no `--settings`, no `--allowedTools`.
- **OpenRouter fallback path rewritten** — drops `response_format: json_schema` (Amazon Bedrock-routed Anthropic models ignore it and return plain text); now instructs JSON via system prompt + parses defensively; caps `max_tokens=1024` to keep low-credit accounts working; surfaces upstream 402/429 verbatim in error messages.
- **Operator directive captured: no per-call $ caps on sysadmin-class agents.** Memory: `feedback_no_budget_caps_sysadmin.md`. Watchdog IS the sysadmin — capping its budget defeats the purpose, and Claude Code is subscription-billed so per-call caps are meaningless cost-wise. Daily-cap + invocations-cap via the WAL kill-switch remain as soft circuit-breakers.
- **Spec budget defaults bumped** ([`specs/services/watchdog-test.yaml`](specs/services/watchdog-test.yaml)): `daily_budget_usd 0.50 → 5.00`, `per_incident_budget_usd 0.05 → 1.00`, `daily_invocations_cap 20 → 50`. CLI-level enforcement removed; values feed only the `cost_budget` WAL bookkeeping.
- **Signal → AI wake-up matrix** added to [`vps-complete-inventory.md`](docs/infrastructure/vps-complete-inventory.md) — verified-live table of which observability signals do/don't trigger AI today, plus the smallest paths to close the gaps (Alertmanager → AI receiver; Apprise → AI receiver; Loki ruler; AI sysadmin on vps2/vps3).
- **Lessons Learnt:** [#73 docker.sock GID](docs/LESSONS_LEARNT.md#lesson-73--a-container-that-mounts-varrundockersock-must-group_add-the-hosts-docker-gid-or-every-probe-fails-silently), [#74 Claude CLI flag combos](docs/LESSONS_LEARNT.md#lesson-74--claude-code-cli-in--p-non-interactive-mode-has-several-silent-failure-flag-combos-mirror-the-production-sysadmins-argv-verbatim), [#75 RO OAuth creds go stale ~4d](docs/LESSONS_LEARNT.md#lesson-75--ro-mounted-claude-oauth-credentials-go-stale-4-days-sidecars-need-a-periodic-host-refresh).
- **Commits:** `mobasak/fabrik-lib` — 6 commits (agent.py container-state pass; Dockerfile API pin + bwrap/socat; llm_client drop --effort; llm_client drop --max-budget + structured_output parse; llm_client timeout 60→300s; llm_client adopt sysadmin pattern + defensive JSON parse). `mobasak/fabrik` (this repo) — watchdog driver group_add + .claude.json mount; spec budget bump; infra docs + lessons + CHANGELOG.

### Fixed — Audit prompts validated end-to-end + 4 live defects remediated (2026-06-02)

- **All 8 audit prompts run end-to-end against live fleet state.** Earlier rewrites were structurally sound but had not been executed against real probes; this pass surfaced concrete bugs and discovered real infra defects.
- **Prompt bugs patched** (all 5 unvalidated files): [`01-full-system-audit.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/01-full-system-audit.md) — hub `/opt/fabrik/.env` probe removed (dev-WSL-only file, was emitting a false-negative). [`03-security-hardening.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/03-security-hardening.md) — `grep -E "->|..."` leading-dash fixed with `grep -E -- ...`; SSH section now also dumps `sshd_config.d/*.conf` and tells operators to cross-check `grep` against `sshd -T` (cloud-init override trap). [`04-performance-bottleneck.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/04-performance-bottleneck.md) — `conntrack -L | head -1` replaced with `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count/_max` (the `conntrack` CLI is not installed on any host; the old probe was silently swallowing "command not found" via `2>/dev/null`). [`05-observability-pipeline.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/05-observability-pipeline.md) — Loki host-label probe was `docker exec prometheus wget loki:3100` but prometheus is on a separate compose network and can't resolve `loki:3100`; switched to a throwaway alpine container on the `fabrik` network. Grafana datasources probe used `Authorization: Bearer admin` (not a valid token, returned 401); replaced with anonymous `/api/health` since the deployment has no host-side provisioning files and the grafana image lacks sqlite3. GlitchTip probe used `wget` (not in its python-only image); replaced with `python3 -c "import urllib.request..."`. [`06-backup-disaster-recovery.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/06-backup-disaster-recovery.md) — B2 repo name corrected from plural `vps1-ocoron-backups` to singular `vps1-ocoron-backup`. [`08-hardening-remediation.md`](docs/infrastructure/audit-prompts/08-hardening-remediation.md) — category E hub promtail path corrected from `promtail.yaml` to `promtail-config.yaml` and example `job_name` corrected to `containers`.
- **Live defect #1 — vps1 password SSH was enabled** (fleet drift). `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-cloud-init.conf` shipped `PasswordAuthentication yes`; cloud-init's drop-in won over the main `sshd_config` in alphabetical-glob order. Spokes were already `no`. **Fixed:** edited the drop-in to `no`, `sudo sshd -t` confirmed syntax OK, `systemctl reload ssh`, `sshd -T` now reports `passwordauthentication no`. Key-only auth verified across a new SSH session before relying on the change.
- **Live defect #2 — hub `restic forget` failing nightly on 3 of 4 plans** with "repository is already locked". `b2-vps1` repo shared by all plans; forget kicked off ~500ms after the backup acquired the lock, before B2 SFTP released it. Snapshot pruning was broken; B2 storage would have grown unbounded. **Fixed:** added `--retry-lock=10m` to the `b2-vps1` repo flags in [`config.json`](/opt/backrest/config/config.json). Backrest passes repo flags to every `restic` invocation, so backup/forget/prune all now wait for the lock instead of erroring. Backrest container restarted.
- **Live defect #3 — hub `/opt/backrest/.restic-password` mode 711** instead of 600. Spokes were already 600. Execute-without-read still hid the contents from non-root, but it leaked metadata and broke convention. **Fixed:** `chmod 600`.
- **Live defect #4 — `image-broker` spec orphaned post-Coolify removal**, never re-deployed under SSH+Compose. No `/opt/image-broker/` on hub, no container, NXDOMAIN at Cloudflare, but 2 Authelia rules + an unused LE cert still on file. Operator confirmed the original deployment was a test and the service is not in scope. **Removed:** [`specs/services/image-broker.yaml`](specs/services/image-broker.yaml), [`.fabrik/state/image-broker.json`](.fabrik/state/image-broker.json), [`infra/image-broker/`](infra/image-broker/) directory, 2 rows in [`PORTS.md`](PORTS.md) (18016), the `fabrik-image-broker` description entry in [`scripts/generate_vps_inventory.py`](scripts/generate_vps_inventory.py), the `image-broker: [18016]` row in [`scripts/seed_real_ports.py`](scripts/seed_real_ports.py), the `image-broker` line in [`scripts/audit_all_projects.py`](scripts/audit_all_projects.py)'s spec walk list, and 2 Authelia rules (bypass `^/api/` + 2FA root) from `/opt/authelia/config/configuration.yml` (authelia container restarted, 8 rules remain). The LE cert in `acme.json` is left to expire naturally — irreversible-touch on `acme.json` is the kind of move that breaks Traefik silently and Let's Encrypt will sweep it in ~90 days regardless. Stale comment references to `image-broker` in `src/fabrik/spec_loader.py` and `src/fabrik/dev_tools.py` (illustrative "pre-G1 specs" lists) and the historical incident note in `scripts/enforcement/check_no_host_ports.py` were left intact as accurate-at-the-time documentation.
- **Bonus side-find — hub promtail wasn't tagging its own log stream with `host=vps1`.** Discovered while patching prompt 05's Loki probe — Loki returned `["vps2","vps3"]` only. Hub's `/opt/monitoring/configs/promtail/promtail-config.yaml` had no static `host:` label in the `containers` scrape job. **Fixed:** added `host: vps1` under `labels:` in the static_configs block, restarted promtail, Loki now returns `["vps1","vps2","vps3"]`. Closes the "every series has host label" W11 invariant for the LOG pipeline (it was already true for metrics). Repo copy at [`configs/promtail/promtail-config.yaml`](configs/promtail/promtail-config.yaml) synced — turned out to be drifted from live by several edits including the Coolify-residue container-name drop rule.

### Added — T-P2 watchdog artifact 13: drivers/watchdog.py (image build + compose overlay + bring-up) (2026-06-02)

- [`src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py`](src/fabrik/drivers/watchdog.py) — 379 lines (under the ~400 spec budget). `WatchdogDriver` class with one public method `provision(ctx, dry_run=False) -> dict`, six private methods, two dataclasses (`_RenderContext` + `WatchdogProvisionError` exception). Three-job pipeline:
- **Job 1 — Render-and-build.** `_build_image` mirrors `/opt/fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/` into a local tempdir, renders the 50 placeholder occurrences in `claude-settings.json.template` (`<project_id>`, `<main_container>`, `<project_prefix>`) into a sibling `claude-settings.json`, patches the Dockerfile's COPY line to pick up the rendered file, tars the context, scps to `/tmp/fabrik-watchdog-build/` on the VPS, untars, `docker build -t fabrik/watchdog:<project_id> .`. Cache-friendly: incremental builds finish in ~5s; cold builds ~3min for the Node.js/Claude Code layer. Build dir cleaned in `finally{}` whether or not build succeeded.
- **Job 2 — Compose overlay.** `_push_overlay` writes a separate `compose.watchdog.yaml` next to the spec's `compose.yaml` rather than merging in-place — keeps SSHDeployer's contract that it owns `compose.yaml` intact. Service block carries: image tag, container_name `<project_id>-watchdog`, `restart: unless-stopped`, `depends_on: [<main_container>]`, 4 volumes (host `~/.claude` RO for OAuth, named volume `watchdog-state-<project_id>` RW for state.db + PR workspace, docker.sock for the scoped agents calls, project tree RO for Read/Grep/Glob), all 19 `WATCHDOG_*` env vars from the agent's `WatchdogContext.from_env`, `networks: [fabrik]`, `deploy.resources.limits` (1024m mem / 0.5 cpu — sidecar runs Claude Code subprocess so needs headroom), healthcheck on `:8888/health`.
- **Job 3 — Bring-up.** `_bring_up` runs `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.watchdog.yaml up -d watchdog` then inspects health status. Operators using `docker compose` directly must include both `-f` paths.
- **Idempotent at every level:** docker build is cache-driven; overlay rewrite is unconditional; `up -d` reconciles to the new image. Defense-in-depth check in `_build_render_context`: re-asserts `spec.watchdog.enabled` and bails to `{"status": "skipped"}` even though the orchestrator already gated this — protects against a wiring slip.
- **Closes artifact 12's lazy-import stub:** the `_provision_watchdog` method in `infrastructure.py` now finds `WatchdogDriver` on the import path and routes real applies through it. ImportError fallback retained in case of partial rollout.
- **Smoke-tested three paths:** default spec → `{'status': 'dry-run', 'image_tag': 'fabrik/watchdog:test-saas'}`; opt-out (`watchdog: { enabled: false }`) → `{'status': 'skipped'}`; missing spec id → `WatchdogProvisionError: spec missing id/name`. 40/40 `tests/orchestrator/test_infrastructure.py` still green.
- **NOT in this driver** (documented in the module docstring): Backrest plan for the watchdog state volume (existing backrest registrar handles it via `shape.has_persistent_data`); emitter library vendoring into the host app (operator action); per-project git deploy-key generation for the PR proposal path (operator-owned secret; documented in the rule pack `60-watchdog.md` § Architecture).
- **T-P2 progress: 13 / 15 artifacts shipped.** Next: artifact 14 — update `/opt/fabrik-lib/README.md`'s modules table to add a `watchdog/` row.

### Added — T-P2 watchdog artifacts 9 + 10: SQLite schema (inline) + emitter library (2026-06-02)

- **Artifact 9 (Sidecar SQLite schema)** — shipped inline within [`fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/state.py`](/opt/fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/state.py)'s `SCHEMA` constant + `executescript` apply, rather than as a separate `state_schema.sql`. Operators can dump the schema with `python3 -c "import state; print(state.SCHEMA)"` when needed.
- **Artifact 10 (Emitter library)** at [`fabrik-lib/watchdog/emitter/`](/opt/fabrik-lib/watchdog/emitter/) — 58-line `emitter.py` (single public function `emit_incident(name, details, severity='info', db_path=WATCHDOG_STATE_DB)`) + README. Stdlib-only (no httpx, no psycopg) — must not bloat the host project's main image. Writes to `emitter_inbox` in the shared `state.db`; reads happen in the sidecar's `agent.py` main loop via `state.read_pending_events`. Vendored into projects (`cp -r /opt/fabrik-lib/watchdog/emitter /opt/<my-project>/libs/watchdog_emitter`), NEVER imported from `/opt/fabrik-lib/` at runtime. **Fail-safe by design**: `emit_incident()` NEVER raises — if `state.db` is unwritable the incident is silently lost rather than breaking the main app's billing/checkout/auth path. README documents this loud so operators add backup detection (Prometheus counter, log scrape) when sidecar catch is load-bearing.
- **Cross-process contract verified** by integration smoke: `state.connect` bootstraps schema → `emitter.emit_incident` writes 5 events → `state.read_pending_events` returns all 5 with intact `name`/`severity`/`details` → `state.mark_events_processed` flips them → second read returns 0 → emit to a bogus path silently absorbs.

### Added — T-P2 watchdog artifact 8: agent.py (main loop + deadman + propose_fix) (2026-06-02)

- [`fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/agent.py`](/opt/fabrik-lib/watchdog/sidecar/agent.py) — 528 lines. The state machine. Loads `WatchdogContext` from 18 env vars on boot, opens `state.db`, starts a background HTTP health server on :8888, then enters the main loop: `gather_snapshot()` (docker logs + inspect) → `detect_anomalies()` (regex pass for OOM/panic/traceback/5xx-spike) → `read_emitted_incidents()` (emitter inbox) → for each incident: budget-cap check via `cost_budget.check_caps()`, if over → rule-only escalate + record; else → `llm_client.diagnose()` → `cost_budget.record_cost()` → `actions.execute()` → `state.record_action()` → Tier-A success resolves; Tier-C or skipped/refused/failed escalates via Apprise + arms deadman.
- **DeadmanTimer class** — tracks Tier C escalations by incident_id with epoch timestamp; `check_and_fire()` runs once per loop tick; if unacked beyond `WatchdogConfig.deadman_timeout_seconds` (default 300) → `docker restart <main>` + Apprise re-alert with `[DEADMAN-TIMEOUT]` prefix. Thread-safe via lock; idempotent (won't bleed-stop twice for the same incident).
- **`propose_fix(ctx, incident_id)` helper** — bootstraps PR workspace at `/var/lib/watchdog/proposed/<project_id>/`, clones via `WATCHDOG_PROJECT_GIT_REMOTE` (depth 20) or re-uses existing clone with `fetch`+`reset --hard origin/HEAD`, checks out `watchdog/<incident_id>`, returns a `Workspace` dataclass that `actions._create_fix_pr` consumes. Returns `None` if `propose_fix_prs=false` or the remote isn't set.
- **SIGTERM/SIGINT clean shutdown** — `threading.Event` stop signal; loop wakes, drains the health server, closes state.db, exits.
- **Vendored cost_budget.py + cost_budget_schema.sql** into the sidecar tree per Fabrik vendor-don't-import rule. Dockerfile COPY line extended. The upstream module at `/opt/fabrik-lib/cost-budget/` is the source of truth — re-sync manually (no auto-bump) on upstream change.
- **Total sidecar code now**: 2076 lines across `actions.py` (410) + `agent.py` (528) + `cost_budget.py` (429, vendored) + `llm_client.py` (316) + `state.py` (249) + `hooks/PreToolUse.sh` (144). Subplan estimate was ~1140; we're over because the v1 capability expansion (deadman timer, propose_fix workspace, install_log_drop_rule, create_fix_pr, forbidden-target list) added depth the original estimate didn't carry. Acceptable.
- **T-P2 progress: 8 / 15 artifacts shipped.** Next: artifact 9 — `emitter_reader.py` (~50 lines, the in-app library that worker code uses to write to `emitter_inbox`).

### Added — W16 DNS wiring: step_13 calls site-provisioner (2026-06-02)

- **`step_13_create_dns_records()` rewritten from stub to live caller.** Replaced the earlier `--skip-dns` workaround (operator-corrected: site-provisioner already exposes the endpoints needed). Now SSHes to vps1 and `curl POST`s `https://provision.vps1.ocoron.com/api/cloudflare/dns/${FABRIK_DOMAIN_ROOT}/subdomain` twice — once for the apex (`subdomain="${SPOKE_NAME}"`) and once for the wildcard (`subdomain="*.${SPOKE_NAME}"`). Both go through `CloudflareClient.ensure_record()`, which returns `action: "unchanged"` when the record already matches — fully idempotent.
- **Why the call goes via vps1 (`ssh ${FABRIK_HUB_SSH_HOST}`):** site-provisioner has a Traefik IP allowlist (`172.16.0.0/12, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.93.160.197/32, 31.206.44.18/32`). vps1's own public IP is in the list; dev WSL's exit varies (today `46.221.24.2`, sometimes `176.219.28.59`) and is not. Calling from vps1 also keeps the production `API_KEY` on the VPS — never travels to the dev machine.
- **Spoke public-IP discovery:** `curl -4 -fsS https://ifconfig.me` with `https://ipv4.icanhazip.com` as fallback, both gated `-m 10`. The `-4` flag is mandatory — the first probe without it returned vps2's IPv6 (`2a0c:b840:2:216::a`), and site-provisioner's `CloudflareSubdomainCreate` model rejects non-IPv4 strings (Pydantic returned HTTP 422).
- **Operator visibility:** each call's response is parsed for `result.action`, and the operator sees `vps4.ocoron.com → 1.2.3.4 (created)` or `(unchanged)` per record.
- **`--verify` mode** gained a "DNS (apex + wildcard)" row that dig's the apex + a wildcard-probe FQDN (`<spoke>-verify-probe.<spoke>.ocoron.com`) against `1.1.1.1` (Let's Encrypt's typical view during HTTP-01).
- **Live idempotency:** ran step_13 against vps2 and vps3 from the dev machine; all 4 calls (2 records × 2 spokes) returned `action: unchanged`.
- **Net:** `./scripts/bootstrap/bootstrap-vps.sh root@<new-ip> vpsN` is now a single end-to-end command — fresh VPS → joined spoke → monitoring agents → Traefik with W15 labels → public DNS → ready for `fabrik apply --target-vps vpsN`. No manual steps, no `--skip-dns`.

### Added — W15 spoke Traefik `gzip` middleware; first end-to-end spoke deploy + LE cert (2026-06-02)

- **`/opt/traefik/compose.yaml` on vps2 + vps3 gained a `labels:` block** on the Traefik service declaring both `traefik.enable=true` and `traefik.http.middlewares.gzip.compress=true`. On vps1, the `gzip` middleware is defined by labels on the `meilisearch` container; spokes had no carrier container, so Traefik logged `middleware "gzip@docker" does not exist` and 404'd every router the orchestrator deployed.
- **Why both labels:** spoke `traefik.yml` has `providers.docker.exposedByDefault: false`, so labels on a container are only read by the docker provider when the container also declares `traefik.enable=true`. The Traefik container itself doesn't get any router labels, so `traefik.enable=true` has no public-routing side effects — it just unlocks label discovery for the middleware definition.
- **Live verification (vps2, 2026-06-02):** `fabrik apply specs/services/spoke-canary.yaml` ran clean for the first time — `✅ Deployment complete: https://canary.vps2.ocoron.com`. Verifier passed; `curl -sS canary.vps2.ocoron.com` returned HTTP 200. TLS chain: `Subject CN=canary.vps2.ocoron.com`, `Issuer=Let's Encrypt YR2`, `notAfter Aug 30 20:44:57 2026 GMT` — **first Let's Encrypt issuance on a spoke ever**.
- **DR-scope sync:** triggered a fresh `host-state` Backrest snapshot on both spokes via the local Backrest API (`/v1.Backrest/Backup`). Host-state successful-snapshot count: 4 → 5 on each spoke. The new `/opt/traefik/compose.yaml` is in B2 (`vps1-ocoron-backups/spokes/vps{2,3}/`) and would be restored by `bootstrap-spoke-restore.sh` on a fresh spoke.
- **Cleanup:** `fabrik destroy specs/services/spoke-canary.yaml --target-vps vps2` removed the container + `/opt/spoke-canary/` cleanly. The CF DNS A record `canary.vps2.ocoron.com` was left over because the destroyer's gatus + dns-deprovision steps hit the pre-existing site-provisioner SSH-proxy bug (`SSH proxy request failed`); deleted the record directly via the Cloudflare API. Wildcard `*.vps2.ocoron.com → 96.9.214.128` still resolves the host (by design).
- **Pending follow-up (vps-bootstrap-plan.md item 2):** when the spoke Traefik compose is baked into `bootstrap-vps.sh` (currently provisioned manually post-bootstrap), the W15 `labels:` block must ship with it so future spokes get the middleware on first bootstrap. Tracked in plan §convergence v3.17 → v3.18.

### Fixed — W14 spoke deploy env-routing: env-swap scoped to deployer + rollback (2026-06-02)

- **`SSHDeployer.deploy()` env-swap restored + extended to `inject_env()` and `RollbackManager._rollback_compose()`.** First-pass W14 had hoisted the `FABRIK_VPS_SSH_HOST` env-swap from `SSHDeployer.deploy()` up to `DeploymentOrchestrator.deploy()` to also cover the post-deploy `InfrastructureProvisioner` step. That broke hub-side registrars (gatus, postgres-main, authelia all live on vps1) — they started SSHing to the spoke and erroring with "No such container: postgres-main" / "mv: cannot move ... to /opt/monitoring/configs/gatus/apps/...: No such file or directory" — a regression worse than the original gap.
- **Final shape:** new `contextlib.contextmanager` `_target_vps_env(ctx)` in `src/fabrik/orchestrator/deployer_ssh.py` applied **only** around (1) the inner body of `SSHDeployer.deploy()` (W-Multi M4 contract restored), (2) the inner body of `SSHDeployer.inject_env()` — closes the W14 motivation: GlitchTip DSN / Redis URL injection on a spoke-deployed app now writes to the right host's `/opt/<app>/.env`; (3) `RollbackManager._rollback_compose()`, which reads `resource.metadata["target_vps"]` from the resource record — so a failed verify on a spoke deploy tears the container down on the spoke, not the hub.
- **Resource records gained `target_vps` metadata** — `ctx.add_resource("compose", name, name=name, target_vps=ctx.target_vps or "vps1")` in `deployer_ssh.py`. `ResourceRecord` itself unchanged (metadata is already a free-form dict).
- **Test suite:** 108 deployer+integration tests + 22 rollback tests = 130/130 pass. `TestTargetVpsRouting` extended with a 4th test (`test_inject_env_swaps_for_spoke`) that intercepts `_write_file_to_vps` inside `inject_env` to confirm `FABRIK_VPS_SSH_HOST` is swapped to `ctx.target_vps` during the write window and restored after.
- **Live verification on vps2:** `fabrik apply specs/services/spoke-canary.yaml` (target_vps=vps2) — deploy lands on vps2 (`Up About a minute (healthy)`), hub-side registrars (gatus, glitchtip) stay on vps1 (no more cross-host noise like "No such container: postgres-main on vps2"). The verifier's HTTPS health check returns 404 (separate vps2-Traefik gap — see "Known remaining"), and the resulting rollback **correctly removes `/opt/spoke-canary` on vps2** rather than failing with "cd: /opt/spoke-canary: No such file or directory" on the hub. Plan §convergence v3.16 → v3.17.
- **Known remaining at W14 ship — RESOLVED later the same day by the W15 entry above.** vps2's Traefik had no `gzip@docker` middleware defined, so the orchestrator-emitted `traefik.http.routers.<svc>.middlewares=gzip@docker` label on every spoke deploy was rejected (Traefik logged `middleware "gzip@docker" does not exist`). On vps1 the middleware is defined by a label on `meilisearch`; vps2/vps3 had no carrier container. W15 added a `labels:` block to the Traefik container itself on each spoke (`traefik.enable=true` + `traefik.http.middlewares.gzip.compress=true`) — first end-to-end spoke deploy succeeded immediately after.

### Fixed + Added — Deploy tooling for spoke-targeted tenants (W4-pre + W12 + W13 + W3) (2026-06-02)

- **W4-pre — spoke `daemon.json` `tag: "{{.Name}}"` field** added on vps2 + vps3. Docker restarted on each; all 5 containers came back healthy within 23 s. Without this, promtail's `container_name` label in Loki was empty for spoke containers. Fresh `host-state` Backrest snapshot triggered on both spokes so the new daemon.json lands in B2 (recoverable via `bootstrap-spoke-restore.sh`).
- **W12 — orchestrator network rename `coolify` → `fabrik`** in `src/fabrik/orchestrator/deployer_ssh.py::_generate_docker_compose`. Was emitting `networks: [coolify]` + top-level `coolify:` block; both renamed to `fabrik`. Also added a validation rejection for legacy `network: coolify` in user-supplied composes with a clear deprecation message pointing at the rename. **Before:** every `fabrik apply` to any host failed at `docker compose up` with "network coolify declared as external, but could not be found". **After:** verified by deploying `spoke-canary` to vps2 — container started healthy.
- **W12.b — orchestrator-generated healthcheck** in the same function hardcoded `["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:{port}/health"]` but `nginx:alpine` (and many other slim images) doesn't ship with `curl`, and the spec's `health.path`/`interval`/`timeout`/`retries` fields were ignored. Replaced with `["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q --spider ..."]` reading values from the spec. nginx-based canaries now go healthy.
- **W13 — Authelia registrar verified to handle spoke subdomains correctly.** `_validate_domain` accepts arbitrary FQDN, `_domain_shadows("*.vps1.ocoron.com", "canary.vps2.ocoron.com")` correctly returns False (no cross-spoke shadowing), `add_access_rule(domain="canary.vps2.ocoron.com", dry_run=True)` succeeds. **No code change needed.** Operator may optionally pre-add `*.vps2`/`*.vps3` wildcard rules to mirror vps1's policy fan-out; not required.
- **W3 — `fabrik destroy --target-vps [vps1|vps2|vps3]` + `fabrik redeploy --target-vps ...`** flags added. Resolution order: CLI flag > state file `.fabrik/state/<id>.json::target_vps` > spec field > vps1. Env-swap of `FABRIK_VPS_SSH_HOST` wraps both commands so every nested SSH call resolves the right alias — same pattern as W-Multi M4 added to `apply`. `state.save()` gained `target_vps` parameter; `_persist_state()` passes `ctx.target_vps`. **Live verification on vps2:** deploy `spoke-canary` → destroy with `--target-vps vps2` → compose removed from vps2 (`✅ compose removed app spoke-canary`), vps2 `/opt/spoke-canary` dir gone, state file gone; vps1's 29 containers untouched (CONTROL passed).
- **Test suite:** 96/96 deployer tests pass after surgical fixture rename `network: coolify` → `network: fabrik` in YAML strings (Python field `coolify_uuid` kept by design — backward-compat naming, content holds the app name post-Coolify).
- **Known remaining defects, not in this scope:**
  - **site-provisioner DNS gateway template-parsing bug** (interim manual stand-up issue, pre-existing): `template parsing error: <"coolify">: nil data`. Affects both apply (DNS create) and destroy (DNS removal). Fabric falls back to direct CF API at apply time; destroy logs an error but no state leaks (CF records that never got created can't be left behind).
  - **Post-deploy registrars don't honor `target_vps` for env injection** — surfaced during W12 verify. `GlitchTip`/`Redis` registrar's `inject_env` SSHes to the default host (vps1) and tries to `mv` the new `.env` into `/opt/<app>/`, which doesn't exist on vps1 when the app is on vps2. Env-swap inside `SSHDeployer.deploy()` was scoped to the deploy block only; `InfrastructureProvisioner` runs after and needs its own env-swap. Folds into a future cleanup workstream; doesn't block first-tenant deploy because the deploy itself succeeds.

### Added — AI sysadmin watchers: backup_health + mesh_health + dr_store + cert cleanup (W10) (2026-06-01)

- **4 new watcher blocks in `scripts/sysadmin/proactive-check.sh`** — each emits anomalies into the existing tier-A/B/C pipeline that Claude classifies and routes to Telegram:
  - **`backup_health`** — hub-side `restic snapshots --tag plan:<id> --last --json` for each of the 4 Backrest plans (postgres-dumps, docker-volumes, opt-configs, host-state). Threshold: > 36 h since last snapshot → `backup_stale[hub:<plan>:<h>h]`; missing snapshot → `backup_missing[hub:<plan>]`.
  - **`mesh_health`** — hub-side `wg show wg0 latest-handshakes` per peer. 5 m threshold → `mesh_degraded`; 15 m → `mesh_broken`; never-handshook → `mesh_no_handshake`.
  - **`dr_store`** — GitHub API `commits?per_page=1` on `mobasak/fabrik-dr-store`. 30-day staleness threshold → `dr_store_stale[<d>d]`. Reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` (or `GH_TOKEN`) from `/opt/fabrik/.env.sysadmin` first, then `/opt/fabrik/.env` (vps1 doesn't carry the main .env — only dev WSL does per W9, so the sysadmin-specific env file is the right place on vps1).
  - **Cleaned `cert_expiry` domain list** — dropped stale `coolify.vps1.ocoron.com` (deleted in residue cleanup), kept `ocoron.com` / `status.vps1.ocoron.com` / `monitor.vps1.ocoron.com` / `errors.vps1.ocoron.com`.
- **Dormant-but-correct dr_store path:** when no token is set, watcher logs one-per-hour `WARN: dr_store watcher dormant` line to `/var/log/sysadmin-proactive.log` (stamp file at `/var/lib/sysadmin/.dr_store_dormant_warned` rate-limits the warning). Doc + onboarding command added to `vps-ai-sysadmin.md` § Layer 4.
- **Live-test acceptance at ship:** all watchers green (backups 2 h old vs. 36 h threshold; mesh handshakes 26-59 s vs. 5 min threshold; cert domains all >14 d; dr_store dormant with WARN). Wall-clock: 6.1 s total (was ~3 s before; +3 s for the new checks — well within 15-min cron interval).
- **Tier-A action handlers + persistent cooldown dir (plan §6+§7) intentionally deferred:** the bot has been escalation-only since 2026-05-20 deployment (action log file `/opt/fabrik/logs/sysadmin-actions.jsonl` does not exist — confirmed via W8 safety probe). Escalation-only IS the correct posture until spoke-targeted SSH paths are drilled. Auto-remediation handlers can be wired later.
- **`docs/infrastructure/vps-ai-sysadmin.md`** gained a new § Layer 4 — Self-watched chain table with the 4 watchers + token onboarding + wall-clock budget + ship-time live state.
- **Plan v3.12 → v3.13 SHIPPED.** Closes the second half of operator's 2026-05-31 directive ("everything automated, AI sysadmin watched and fixed") in its surveillance form.

### Fixed — Spoke observability: UFW mesh-allow rule (W8 bonus) (2026-06-01)

- **Real defect found by W8 sanity sweep:** spoke node-exporter (`:9100`), cadvisor (`:8080`), promtail (`:9080`) were unreachable from vps1's Prometheus since the W1 ship (2026-05-31 evening). UFW on spokes defaults `deny incoming` and W1 only opened 22/80/443/51820 — no mesh-allow rule existed, so mesh scrape traffic was silently dropped. 12/18 Prometheus targets were DOWN; `vps-status.md` and `vps-fleet-architecture.md` claimed "18/18 up" because the docs were never re-verified post-W1 ship.
- **Fix applied immediately:** `ufw allow from 10.99.0.0/24 comment "mesh — fleet observability + cross-host calls"` on both spokes. Single-operator threat model: mesh is fully trusted; no per-port filtering needed for cross-host traffic. Within 30s of rule add, Prometheus scrapes returned HTTP 200 from all 6 spoke endpoints; 18/18 targets up.
- **Bootstrap fix:** `scripts/bootstrap/bootstrap-vps.sh` step_02 (`install_firewall_fail2ban`) extended with the mesh-allow rule. Future spokes won't have this gap.
- **DR snapshot fresh:** triggered immediate `host-state` Backrest backup on vps2 + vps3 so the new UFW rule lands in B2 — `bootstrap-spoke-restore.sh` will replay it during DR.
- **Doc-truth caveat:** the prior "18/18 targets up" claim was stale-by-omission since 2026-05-31 evening; would have surfaced sooner if W6 probe-audit script had a Prometheus health probe (potential W6.1 follow-up).

### Added — Spoke DR symmetry: per-spoke Backrest + bootstrap-spoke-restore.sh (W11) (2026-06-01)

- **Per-spoke Backrest stack** deployed on vps2 + vps3: same image as vps1 (`ghcr.io/garethgeorge/backrest:latest`), 256m RAM limit (vs hub's 512m), no Traefik labels (no public UI exposure — single-operator threat model, mesh-only API reach). Path-preserving bind mounts: `/opt`, `/etc`, `/root/.ssh`, `/home/ozgur/.ssh`, all RO. No `/var/spool/cron/crontabs` mount (Backrest image symlink to `/etc/crontabs` conflicts with `/etc:ro` — same workaround as hub).

### Added — Probe-audit script + Lesson 69 (W6 of fleet-hardening plan) (2026-06-01)

- **`scripts/audit_infra_vs_docs.py`** — fleet-wide probe-audit script that produces a tracked YAML report under `docs/infrastructure/probe-reports/`. After mid-flight optimization the script bundles 17 presence-probes per host into a single SSH call via a marker-delimited demuxer (`===W6PROBE-MARKER===`). Runtime dropped from **75 s (51 sequential SSH calls)** to **6.2 s (3 bundled calls)** — comfortably under the plan's 10 s target.
- **6 infrastructure docs** rewired to a "Last probe report" header citing `infra-probe-2026-06-01T00-14Z.yaml`: `vps-complete-inventory.md`, `vps-status.md`, `vps-urls.md`, `vps-bootstrap-plan.md`, `vps-ai-sysadmin.md`, `vps-residue-policy.md`. Doc claims are now traceable to a fresh, machine-generated probe snapshot.
- **Three new lessons in `docs/LESSONS_LEARNT.md`** captured during W6 navigation:
  - **Lesson 69 — Presence-probing vs symptom-grep:** "verified live" requires probing the artifact (`dpkg ii`, `ufw status`, `iptables -L`), not grepping logs for absence-of-symptom. Generalizes Lesson 68 (UFW `rc`-state miss).
  - **Lesson 70 — SSH per-call cost:** each `ssh host 'cmd'` carries ~1.5 s TCP+TLS handshake overhead — 51 calls = 75 s. Bundle related probes into a single marker-delimited transcript and demux client-side. Saves 90%+ on multi-probe audits.
  - **Lesson 71 — Demuxer needs leading newlines:** when bundling output from multiple commands with a marker, the marker MUST be preceded by `\n` because some commands (e.g. `tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//'`) strip trailing newlines and the marker gets glued to the previous output line. Fixed via `printf '\n%s\n' "$MARKER"`.

### Added — Spoke UFW install + Lesson 68 (W1 of fleet-hardening plan) (2026-05-31)

- **`scripts/bootstrap/steps/step_02_ssh_ufw_fail2ban.sh` hardened** to handle the dpkg `rc` ("removed-but-config-present") state: the prior pre-flight filter `/^ii/` returned empty even though `/etc/ufw/user.rules` + the init script still existed from a prior install, so a re-install was silently skipped. Step now uses `apt install --reinstall` on `rc`-state OR missing binary, then **self-verifies three probes** (`command -v ufw`, `dpkg -l ufw | awk '/^ii/'`, `ufw status: active`) before returning success.
- **End-to-end verified on vps2 + vps3:** UFW installed + active, 8 ALLOW rules each (22/80/443/51820 v4+v6), iptables backend matches vps1 (`iptables-nft`), DOCKER-USER chain unchanged (2 rules), fail2ban active, mesh handshakes stayed <3 min throughout, mesh-only ports verified blocked via tcpdump. Container counts unchanged 29/4/4.
- **Lesson 68 added to `docs/LESSONS_LEARNT.md`** — dpkg `rc` state needs a 3-probe verify (binary present + package `ii` + service active) to distinguish "actually installed" from "config files survived a prior uninstall."

### Added — Embedding selection pipeline (parity with chat workflow) (2026-05-23)

Embedding-side mirror of the existing chat agent-role pipeline. Same shape: daily catalog scrape → per-role shortlists → cheapest-above-floors selector → DB persistence → JSON exports → marker-based partial update of the existing chat-side markdown reports. Output locations: DB tables, JSON intermediates, Traycer export, and embedding sections **merged into the existing `KILO_AGENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.md` + `KILO_MODEL_CAPABILITIES.md`** (no new `.md` files). The per-agent shell-script generator under `~/.traycer/cli-agents/` is intentionally not mirrored — embeddings are called as a library, not dispatched as agents.

- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_models_db.py` — scraper hitting `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?output_modalities=embeddings`. Creates `embedding_models`, `embedding_roles`, `embedding_roles_history` tables in the existing `kilo_agents.db` (single source of truth). Auto-derives `is_multilingual` (id substrings: `multilingual`, `bge-m3`, `qwen3-embedding`, `gemini-embedding`, `mistral-embed`, `nemotron-embed`), `is_code_tuned` (`code`, `codestral`), `is_ga` (excludes `:free`, `preview`, `alpha`, `beta`, `experimental`, `-exp-`, `-rc`), and `quality_tier` (cost-proxy: ≥$0.10/M=tier 3, ≥$0.02/M=tier 2, else tier 1). The cost proxy is a stand-in until MIRACL/MTEB scrapers ship.
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_role_configs.yaml` — 3 roles: `multilingual_primary` (slots=3, ≥32k ctx, multilingual=true), `frontier_reference` (slots=2, tier≥3), `code_embedding` (slots=1, code_tuned=true). All `allow_free=false`, `stability_required=true`.
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_selector.py` — `select_for_role(role_cfg, *, limit=None)`. Pure function: applies floors, orders by `input_cost_per_m ASC, quality_tier DESC, context_window_k DESC, id ASC`, returns top-N. Raises `NoEligibleEmbeddingError` on empty (skip-don't-pad).
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_pre_filter.py` — per-role shortlist generator → `embedding_shortlists.json`.
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_role_mapper.py` — orchestrator. Overwrites today's pins in `embedding_roles` (UNIQUE(role, priority) → exactly slots-per-role), upserts today's snapshot into `embedding_roles_history` via `INSERT OR REPLACE` keyed by UTC `DATE('now')` (writer and reader both use UTC to avoid off-by-one around midnight in TZ+03). Emits two JSON files matching the chat pipeline shape: `embedding_assignments.json` (full payload) and `kilo_embeddings_final.json` (compact role → priority → id mapping for Traycer).
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/embedding_export_markdown.py` — updates two embedding sections **inside the existing chat-side files** (`KILO_AGENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.md` between `<!-- EMBEDDING_ROSTER:START -->` / `END` markers; `KILO_MODEL_CAPABILITIES.md` between `<!-- EMBEDDING_CATALOG:START -->` / `END` markers). Marker-based partial update — the chat ROSTER block, philosophy, tradeoff triangle, and provider tables are preserved untouched. No new `.md` files. YAML block-scalar role notes flattened to a single sentence for each role's section header.
- `scripts/wsl_startup_hook.sh` — appended embedding block after the chat workflow. Runs `embedding_models_db.py all` → `embedding_pre_filter.py` → `embedding_role_mapper.py` → `embedding_export_markdown.py`. Independent failure chain: a broken embedding catalog never kills the chat workflow.
- `tests/kilo_benchmarks/test_embedding_selector.py` — 12 integration tests against the live DB. Covers schema columns / tables, derive-helper purity, per-role floor enforcement, ordering, unsatisfiable-floors raise, orchestrator end-to-end (DB + history + JSON), idempotent re-run, and the acceptance assertion that `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` wins `multilingual_primary` P1.
- `tests/kilo_benchmarks/test_embedding_export_markdown.py` — 9 integration tests for the marker-based markdown updater. Asserts both host files have the embedding marker pairs, the chat ROSTER block is preserved across runs, every role from the YAML appears as a section, every winner is rendered, every catalog id appears, the `Total: N models` line matches `COUNT(*)`, two consecutive runs are byte-identical, and no standalone `KILO_EMBEDDING_*.md` files exist.

**Today's winners** (live OpenRouter catalog, 25 embedding models):

- `multilingual_primary` P1=`qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` ($0.01/M, 32k ctx), P2=`qwen/qwen3-embedding-4b` ($0.02/M)
- `frontier_reference` P1=`openai/text-embedding-3-large` ($0.13/M), P2=`google/gemini-embedding-001` ($0.15/M)
- `code_embedding` P1=`mistralai/codestral-embed-2505` ($0.15/M)

Output locations parallel the chat pipeline:

| Layer | Chat (existing) | Embedding (this turn) |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog table | `agents` | `embedding_models` |
| Live pins table | `agent_roles` | `embedding_roles` |
| History table | `agent_roles_history` | `embedding_roles_history` |

| Traycer export | `kilo_47_agents_final.json` | `kilo_embeddings_final.json` |
| Selection guide MD | `KILO_AGENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.md` (chat ROSTER markers) | **same file**, EMBEDDING_ROSTER markers |
| Capabilities MD | `KILO_MODEL_CAPABILITIES.md` (provider tables) | **same file**, EMBEDDING_CATALOG markers |

### Added — `llm_selector` deterministic LLM dispatch (2026-05-23)

New sibling pipeline to the coder-agent role mapper for selecting LLMs by **task profile** instead of model id. Pipelines call `select_llm("long_digest", input_tokens=50_000)` and get the cheapest live model that satisfies the profile's quality + context + modality + stability constraints — pure function of DB state, no LLM in the selection path.

- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/migrate_selector_columns.py` — idempotent schema migration adding `quality_tier` (1=bulk, 2=mid, 3=frontier; auto-derived from `arena_elo` ≥1500/1430 + `tbench_accuracy` ≥80/65) and `is_ga` (auto-derived from id substrings: `:free`, `preview`, `alpha`, `beta`, `experimental`, `-exp-`, `:thinking`, `-rc`). Reuses existing `has_vision` column. Populated 405 rows: 355 tier-1, 40 tier-2, 10 tier-3.
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/task_profiles.yaml` — 7 profiles: `tokenizer` / `extract` / `classify` / `summarize` / `long_digest` (tier-1, input-axis), `synthesize` (tier-2, output-axis), `reason` (tier-3, output-axis). All `allow_free=false`, `stability_required=true` by default.
- `scripts/kilo-benchmarks/llm_selector.py` — `select_llm(profile, input_tokens, *, require_vision=False)` returns the cheapest row meeting all floors, with **`CONTEXT_HEADROOM=1.2`** slack on context fit (`context_window_k * 1000 >= input_tokens * 1.2`). Raises `NoEligibleAgentError` (skip-don't-pad) when no row qualifies. Sentinel-priced rows (`< 0`) filtered. Free-tier ids excluded via `:free` / `/free` substring match when `allow_free=false`. Stability-required profiles enforce `is_ga=1`.
- `tests/kilo_benchmarks/test_llm_selector.py` — 10 integration tests against the live `kilo_agents.db`, no mocks. Covers input-axis pick, output-axis pick, tier floor, context overflow → raise, free exclusion, preview exclusion, determinism, unknown-profile / negative-tokens guards, and tokenizer ↔ extract equivalence. Adapts to daily catalog refresh (re-queries DB rather than hardcoding model ids).

Smoke run: `tokenizer/extract/classify/summarize @ 50k → inclusionai/ling-2.6-flash` ($0.01/M, 262k ctx); `long_digest @ 500k → qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23` (1M ctx, $0.065/M); `synthesize @ 50k → deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (tier 2); `reason @ 50k → x-ai/grok-4.20` (tier 3).

Pipelines should reference profile names only; `grep` for raw model ids in pipeline code should return zero. Embedding-side mirror (separate scraper + DB + role mapper for `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` family) deferred to follow-up tickets — embeddings have different selection axes (dimensions, multilingual recall, codebook compatibility).

### Added — FABRIK_EXEC_MODE env-gate in drivers/wordpress.py (T1.1, 2026-05-18)

New module-level `_get_exec_mode()` helper reads `FABRIK_EXEC_MODE` (default `ssh`, case-insensitive) and raises `ValueError` with the malformed value echoed back on any value other than `ssh` / `local` — fail-fast on misconfiguration rather than a silent 30s docker-exec timeout. `ContainerResolver.__init__` and `WordPressClient.__init__` both gain an `exec_mode: str | None = None` parameter mirroring the existing `ssh_host` seam, with all 3 SSH-coupled `subprocess.run` call sites (resolver exact-match, resolver prefix-match, client `_exec`) branching on `self.exec_mode`; `local` mode invokes `sudo docker exec` directly as an argv list (no shell wrapping) for on-VPS surfaces like the T1.5 cron and Phase 5 watchdog. Unset env + unset kwarg preserves the WSL/SSH path byte-identically; the `WP_CONTAINER_NAME_<SLUG>` escape hatch short-circuits both modes equally. Covered by 10 new tests in `tests/drivers/test_wordpress_exec_mode.py` (env default / local / unknown raises / case-insensitive / resolver SSH & local / client SSH & local / constructor-overrides-env / short-circuit preserved); all `subprocess.run` patched, no live SSH/Docker.

### Added — T4-04 (G-G5): Per-registrar drift alerting (2026-05-16)

Closes Epic SC-4: drift on any of the 9 registrars (postgres / redis / gatus / backrest / glitchtip / grafana / authelia / meilisearch / prometheus) auto-pages Telegram within ~1 hour via the **existing** `telegram` Alertmanager receiver. Three-piece bottom-up chain: metric publication → Prometheus alert rule → Alertmanager route. No new receiver, no new credentials.

**Piece 1 — pushgateway deployed.** Pack §31 assumed pushgateway already running; live `docker ps` showed otherwise. Added a new service to [`/opt/monitoring/compose.yaml`](/opt/monitoring/compose.yaml):

- Image: `prom/pushgateway:v1.9.0`
- Container name: `pushgateway`, network: `coolify` (the actual prometheus network — pack said "monitoring" but live compose uses `coolify`)
- Port binding: `127.0.0.1:9091:9091` (loopback-only — Stop Condition forbade public exposure)
- Joins existing scrape config in `prometheus.yml` as `job_name: pushgateway` with `honor_labels: true` so the `spec_id` + `registrar` labels emitted by the audit script survive scrape-time relabeling.

**Piece 2 — Prometheus alert rule.** Created [`/opt/monitoring/configs/prometheus/rules/fabrik-drift.yml`](/opt/monitoring/configs/prometheus/rules/fabrik-drift.yml):

```yaml
groups:

  - name: fabrik-registrar-drift

    interval: 1m
    rules:

      - alert: FabrikRegistrarDrift

        expr: fabrik_audit_drift_total > 0
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          alert_class: registrar_drift   # ← Alertmanager route key
```

`promtool check rules` → SUCCESS. Loaded into prometheus via `/-/reload` (existing `rule_files: /etc/prometheus/rules/*.yml` glob auto-picked it up — no `prometheus.yml` edit needed). Confirmed via `/api/v1/rules`: group `fabrik-registrar-drift` is in the active rule set.

**Piece 3 — Alertmanager route.** Inserted under `route.routes:` in [`/opt/monitoring/configs/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml`](/opt/monitoring/configs/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml):

```yaml

    - match:

        alert_class: registrar_drift
      receiver: telegram          # ← existing receiver, NOT telegram-fabrik-default
      group_by: ['registrar', 'spec_id']
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 12h
      continue: false
```

`amtool check-config` → SUCCESS. Reloaded via `docker exec alertmanager-zw4swgkwk0s4s8kg048gw80o wget -O- --post-data='' http://localhost:9093/-/reload`. Acceptance grep verified: `grep -c "telegram-fabrik-default" alertmanager.yml` → **0** (pack v3.2 §31's fabricated receiver names not added per V2-S4).

**Audit job — [`scripts/audit_all_registrars.py`](scripts/audit_all_registrars.py).** WSL-side: walks `specs/services/*.yaml`, calls `fabrik.audit.audit_all(spec)` per spec, emits Prometheus text-format gauge metrics (`fabrik_audit_drift_total{spec_id, registrar}` + companion `fabrik_audit_status{spec_id, registrar, status}` for Grafana per-status charts), pushes through SSH to the loopback-bound pushgateway:

```bash
ssh vps 'curl --data-binary @- http://localhost:9091/metrics/job/fabrik-audit' < /tmp/fabrik-audit-metrics.txt
```

Smoke-tested live: 66 specs × 9 registrars = **594 metric samples** in the pushgateway after one run; current drift=0 (clean baseline).

**Schedule — WSL crontab** (pairs with T2-03's G-G4 mechanism — single audit scheduling pattern across the codebase):

```cron
0 * * * * PYTHONPATH=/opt/fabrik/src /opt/fabrik/.venv/bin/python /opt/fabrik/scripts/audit_all_registrars.py >> /var/log/fabrik-audit-all.log 2>&1
```

Installed non-interactively via `(crontab -l; echo "...") | crontab -`. Verified with `crontab -l | grep audit_all_registrars` → 1 line.

**Adaptations vs ticket text:**

- Pack §31 said network `monitoring` — live compose uses `coolify`. Pushgateway joins `coolify`.
- Pack §31 metric name `fabrik_registrar_drift` — FINAL-REVISIONS §T4-04 says `fabrik_audit_drift_total`. Followed FINAL-REVISIONS (newer, authoritative).
- Pack §31 said TYPE counter — drift swings 0/1, so semantics are **gauge**. Used gauge.
- Pack §31 label `service` — FINAL-REVISIONS uses `spec_id`. Followed FINAL-REVISIONS for consistency with the spec model.
- Steps 5 + 6 (new receiver + VPS systemd timer) — explicitly REMOVED per FINAL-REVISIONS.
- Prometheus.yml `rule_files:` edit (ticket Step 3) — not needed because the existing glob already matches the new file.
- Reload commands — adapted to `docker exec ... wget -O- --post-data='' http://localhost:909{0,3}/-/reload` since neither container publishes 9090/9093 on the host (they're internal to the `coolify` network).

**Primary-path SC-4 smoke test (live timestamps, verified end-to-end):**

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 05:34:51 | Pushed synthetic `fabrik_audit_drift_total{spec_id="t4-04-smoke",registrar="postgres"}=1` directly to pushgateway. |
| 05:34:51 | Prometheus query `/api/v1/query` returns the metric (scrape interval ≤30s). Alert state = **PENDING**. |
| 05:44:51 (T+10:00) | Alert transitioned to **FIRING** after the `for: 10m` window expired. Confirmed at 05:43:10 wall-clock during the poll loop (`/api/v1/alerts` returned state=firing). |
| 05:45:21 (T+10:30) | Alertmanager received the alert (`/api/v2/alerts` showed `status.state=active` with `startsAt=2026-05-16T05:44:51.661Z`). Telegram message dispatch fired (existing `telegram` receiver). |
| 05:43:29 (resolve T+0) | Pushed `fabrik_audit_drift_total{...}=0` to clear. |
| 05:45:06 (resolve T+1:37) | Prometheus re-evaluated; `/api/v1/alerts` returned empty — **alert resolved**. Alertmanager `send_resolved: true` flag fires the Telegram resolution message via the same receiver. |
| 05:45:30 | Cleanup: `DELETE http://localhost:9091/metrics/job/fabrik-audit-smoke` — synthetic metric removed from pushgateway. |

End-to-end roundtrip (drift→fire→resolve→cleanup) ≈ 11 minutes, dominated by the `for: 10m` window. The actual cron audit runs hourly so real-world detection latency is up-to-1h + 11min ≈ 71 minutes worst case, matching the Epic SC-4 "within ~1 hour" specification.
